items.title: Slow resolution from Azure DevOps feed
items.reason: Canonical match: astral-sh/uv#11379 covers Azure Artifacts without PEP 658, ranged GETs that work after redirects, uv's unsupported-range warning, and fallback to streamed wheel metadata.

items.title: Fix wheel metadata reads after redirects
items.reason: astral-sh/uv#21347 provides a focused integration test reproducing the redirect failure, although its proposed use of the HEAD response URL remains under review.

items.title: uv's HEAD-based range detection for wheel metadata is inconsistent with RFC 9110 and misclassifies GAR wheel URLs
items.reason: Adjacent report with the same fallback when PEP 658 is unavailable, but its HEAD response lacks a usable range signal; the present reproduction has a successful redirected HEAD followed by failed range GET redirect handling.

items.title: Support netrc and same-origin credential propagation on index redirects
items.reason: Introduced uv's manual redirect wrapper; maintainer analysis on astral-sh/uv#21347 identifies the range reader's loss of that wrapper as the apparent regression path.

items.title: Upgrade `async_http_range_reader` to v0.8.0
items.reason: Historical fix preserving the original URL for range GETs because some indexes produce different method-specific signed URLs for HEAD and GET, constraining the proposed fix.

items.title: Stream zip archive when fetching non-range-request metadata
items.reason: Establishes that range failure streams until METADATA rather than necessarily saving the complete wheel, although it may still transfer most of the archive.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests. Literal searches covered “range requests,” “range request,” “PEP 658,” “full wheel,” “whole wheels,” “Accept-Ranges,” “Content-Range,” “Azure Artifacts,” and warning/fallback terminology. Conceptual and fix-oriented searches covered lazy wheels, remote wheel metadata, streamed fallback, redirects, authentication middleware, index capability caching, and method-specific signed URLs. Inspected the comment and reference chains around astral-sh/uv#11379, astral-sh/uv#21347, astral-sh/uv#18998, astral-sh/uv#14126, astral-sh/uv#7226, astral-sh/uv#3460, astral-sh/uv#2843, and astral-sh/uv#1792. astral-sh/uv#18998 was ruled out as the canonical duplicate because its failure is HEAD-based capability detection. astral-sh/uv#5073 was ruled out because it concerns generic streamed-fallback performance rather than redirect handling on a range-capable feed.

type_reason: astral-sh/uv#11379 remains open and tracks the same Azure Artifacts metadata-resolution fallback: no PEP 658 metadata, working ranged GETs after redirects, and uv treating ranges as unsupported. The new issue adds uv 0.12.7 confirmation and a focused reproduction, but discussion can be centralized in the existing tracker. The underlying behavior is a bug and may be a redirect-handling regression, but an open issue already tracks that regression shape.
summary: astral-sh/uv#11379 is the same open Azure redirect/range-metadata problem. astral-sh/uv#21347 adds a direct reproduction and proposed fix, while related history explains why redirect and signed-URL handling require care.
